title: Realm makes room for touch controls
thesis: The opening needs clear, responsive controls before more visual experiments.
summary: Phone controls now clear the minimap and touch tooltips. Closed Sprite Lab work waits until it is opened. Real opening delivery and Save → reload → Continue checks pass.

comparisons.title: The build bar gets its space back
comparisons.caption: Separate detached worktrees; identical named seed, paused tick 120, camera, 390 × 844 viewport and serialized world hash. Before: minimap overlap of 67 pixels and a tooltip lingering after a Farm tap. After: 8 pixels of clearance and no touch tooltip.

before.alt: Before: selected Farm with a lingering tooltip and minimap overlapping the phone build bar.

after.alt: After: same Farm selection, no tooltip and minimap above the phone build bar.

changes.title: Controls respect the input device
changes.body: Mouse hover still shows help. Touch selection clears the tooltip. The minimap follows the measured build-bar height.

changes.title: Sprite Lab waits until opened
changes.body: Ordinary startup now creates zero lab rows and makes zero lab-source requests, compared with 224 rows and two requests before. First-open, reopen and deep-link browser checks pass.

changes.title: The opening stays playable
changes.body: Tutorial guidance recognizes an existing Farm. Real build-bar clicks create a Farm and Granary, physical food reaches storage, and Save → reload → Continue restores the exact saved tick.

builderNote.quote: The opening needs clear, responsive controls before more visual experiments.
builderNote.context: Implementation note from this recovery pass, not an owner endorsement. Working branch; not merged or deployed.

proof.label: Passed
proof.value: Desktop and phone opening tutorial, real touch cancellation, tooltip input, Sprite Lab opening, real food delivery, citizen food routes, browser save shell, source save continuity, module graph and core purity.

proof.label: Limits
proof.value: Isolated headless Chrome used file-origin loading. Deployed HTTP behavior and the full release suite remain unverified. Measurements are not a timing benchmark.
